changes.text: 居里夫妇把制备镭的方法毫无保留地公开，镭工业因此自由发展；他们自己却长期缺钱、缺场地。1921年赠镭之前，梅洛尼探访时，她的实验室仍设备不足；靠美国妇女募捐，居里夫人才得到一克镭。这是一笔两边都有分量的账。

The Curies published their method for preparing radium without reserve, and the radium industry grew freely on it. They themselves long went without money and without a proper workplace. When Meloney visited, before the 1921 gift, Marie Curie's laboratory still lacked sufficient equipment, and a subscription raised by American women finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands. It is a ledger with weight on both sides.
1921年5月20日，白宫。美国妇女把一克镭赠给它的发现者，可镭本身并不在现场。哈定总统交给居里夫人的是一把小金钥匙，用来打开运送镭的箱子。装镭的管子还在“局”里，那里的官员主动提出代为测量、装箱并送上船。

May 20, 1921, the White House. The women of America gave a gram of radium to its discoverer, but the radium itself was not in the room. What President Harding placed in Marie Curie's hands was a small golden key, the one that opened the casket devised for transporting the radium. The tubes of radium were still at the Bureau, whose officials had kindly offered to make the measurements and to take care of the packing and delivery to the ship.
一克镭的市价是十万美元。而制备镭的方法，是她和皮埃尔·居里多年前毫无保留地公开的，镭工业正靠它发展起来、高价卖货。公开了方法的她，实验室里那点镭当时只用于为医院提取射气；梅洛尼发起募捐，希望借此让她把研究继续下去。这笔账，她在书里一项一项算过。

A gram of radium then sold for one hundred thousand dollars. The process for preparing it had been published years earlier, without reserve, by Marie Curie and Pierre Curie, and the radium industry was now thriving on that very process and selling its product at a high price. She had helped give the method away, yet the radium in her laboratory was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use, and Meloney set out to raise a subscription to enable her to go on with her work. In her book she worked through that account line by line.
事情要从1890年代末的巴黎说起。居里夫妇想把一种新放射性物质提纯到能确认是新元素，可他们缺合适的工作场所、缺人手，也缺钱。沥青铀矿很贵，他们买不起足够的量。当时这种矿物的主要来源在波希米亚的圣约阿希姆斯塔尔，奥地利政府在那里经营一座提铀的矿。矿上的残渣还从没用过，他们相信镭和一部分钋就在残渣里。靠维也纳科学院的影响，他们以优惠价拿到几吨残渣。起初的费用出自自己的积蓄，后来才得到少量补助。

The story begins in Paris in the late 1890s. The Curies wanted to purify a new radioactive substance far enough to be sure it was a new element, and they lacked a proper place to work in, personnel and money. Pitchblende was an expensive mineral, and they could not afford to buy a sufficient quantity. At that time the principal source of this mineral was at St. Joachimsthal in Bohemia, where the Austrian government worked a mine for the extraction of uranium. Its residues had so far not been used at all, and they believed the radium, and part of the polonium, would be found in them. Through the influence of the Vienna Academy of Sciences they secured several tons of the residues at an advantageous price. In the beginning the costs came out of their own pockets; only later were they given a few subventions and some help from outside sources.
这两年他们几乎无人相助。这里要补一句：实验室杂工珀蒂常在能挤出的时间里搭手；1898年，学校的实验室主任之一贝蒙临时帮过忙；1900年前后，青年化学家德比埃尔纳加入。分工后皮埃尔研究镭的性质，她负责把镭提纯成纯盐。她一次处理多达二十公斤材料，棚里堆满沉淀物和液体；她要搬运容器、转移液体，再用铁棒连续几小时搅拌铸铁锅里沸腾的物料。

For two years they worked there practically unaided. One qualification: the laboratory helper, Petit, kept lending a hand in whatever time he could spare; G. Bemont, one of the laboratory chiefs at the School, gave temporary help in 1898; and around 1900 the young chemist André Debierne joined them. Once the work was divided, Pierre studied the properties of radium while Marie Curie pushed ahead with the chemical experiments aimed at preparing pure radium salts. She worked with as much as twenty kilogrammes of material at a time, until the hangar was full of great vessels of precipitates and liquids: moving the containers about, transferring the liquids, and stirring the boiling material in the cast-iron basin with an iron bar, for hours at a stretch.

这时日内瓦方面来请皮埃尔：那里物质条件更好，还能过上近似乡居的宁静生活。按居里夫人的记述，这个决定很艰难，皮埃尔动了心。最后让他定下来不去的，是他们正对镭做的研究，他怕这样的变动打断它。此时，索邦为医科学生而设的P.C.N.物理教席正好空缺。他申请后，在庞加莱影响下获聘；她则受托在塞夫尔的女子师范学校讲物理课。他们留在巴黎，收入增加了，工作却更难：皮埃尔要兼两处课，其中学生众多的P.C.N.教学让他非常疲惫。

Then Geneva came calling for Pierre, offering material advantages and the opportunity of a life comparable in its tranquillity with that in the country. In Marie Curie's account the decision was a grave one, and Pierre was tempted. What finally settled it was the radium research itself, since he feared the interruption that such a change must involve. At this moment the chair of physics in the Sorbonne's P.C.N. course was vacant; this was the physics, chemistry and natural history curriculum compulsory for medical students. He applied, and was appointed through the influence of Henri Poincaré, who was anxious to free him from the necessity of quitting France. Marie Curie was given charge of the physics lectures at the Normal School for Girls at Sèvres. They stayed in Paris and their income increased, but working conditions grew harder: Pierre was doing double teaching, and the P.C.N., with its very large number of students, fatigued him greatly.

新职位不带实验室。在索邦设于居维叶街12号、供P.C.N.教学用的附属楼里，他只有一间小办公室和一个工作间。他想接收学生做研究，就去争取更大的场地。照她的说法，做过这类事的人知道那是一堵怎样的墙：公文、登门、请求，有一点成果都要付出很多，这些事彻底让他厌倦和沮丧。同时，没有工业手段处理原料，研究也推不动了。1899年，皮埃尔借中央化学产品公司的一处现成设施组织第一次工业试验，技术细节由德比埃尔纳安排得很成功；这种需要特殊小心的活儿，还得专门训练人手。

The new post came without a laboratory. In the annex at 12 rue Cuvier that served as teaching quarters for the P.C.N., all he had at his disposition was a little office and a single work room. He meant to receive students and start them in research, so he took steps to find larger working quarters. Anyone who has taken similar steps knows the wall of financial and administrative obstacles he was throwing himself against: the official letters, the visits, the requests, and what even the least success entailed. It all thoroughly wearied and discouraged him. Meanwhile the research could not advance without industrial means of treating the raw material. In 1899 Pierre Curie organized a first industrial experiment, using for it a chance installation placed at his disposition by the Central Society of Chemical Products, with which he had dealt over the construction of his balances. The technical details were arranged very successfully by André Debierne, and the operations brought good results, though a special crew had to be trained for chemical work that demanded special precautions.

梅洛尼（本书引言作者）曾在纽约发起这次募捐。她见到居里夫人时，居里夫人说美国约有五十克镭，巴尔的摩四克、丹佛六克、纽约七克；在法国，她的实验室的镭几乎不超过一克。梅洛尼惊问她只有一克吗，她纠正说，那不是她的，而是属于她的实验室。梅洛尼那一周得知，一克镭市价十万美元。她的实验室虽然几乎是新楼，设备并不够用，那里的镭当时只用于为医院提取射气治疗癌症。梅洛尼原想几周后到纽约时，找十位女士各出一万美元买下一克，免去公开募捐的声势，结果只找到一两位。后来是十万名妇女和一批男士下决心要把钱募齐，不到一年基金就募成了。据居里夫人自己的记述，一个由几位知名女士和杰出科学家组成的委员会收到一些重要捐赠，并发起公众认捐，许多妇女组织、尤其是大学和俱乐部纷纷响应，不少捐款来自受益于镭疗法的人。就这样，集成了超过十万美元的居里夫人镭基金。

Meloney, who later wrote the book's introduction, had launched the subscription in New York. When Meloney met her, Marie Curie said that America had about fifty grammes of radium: four of these in Baltimore, six in Denver, seven in New York, and on she went, naming the location of every grain. And in France? "My laboratory," she said, "has hardly more than a gramme." Meloney, astonished, exclaimed that she had only a gramme. "I? Oh, I have none," Marie Curie corrected. "It belongs to my laboratory." That week Meloney learned that the market price of a gramme of radium was one hundred thousand dollars. She also learned that Marie Curie's laboratory, although practically a new building, was without sufficient equipment, and that the radium held there was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use in cancer treatment. When she arrived in New York a few weeks afterwards, Meloney had hoped to find ten women to subscribe ten thousand dollars each and buy a gramme without the publicity of a general campaign. She found one or two. There were not ten women to buy that gramme of radium, but there were a hundred thousand women and a group of men determined that the money must be raised, and in less than a year the fund had been raised. In Marie Curie's own account, a committee including several prominent women and distinguished scientific men received some important gifts and made an appeal for a public subscription. A great number of women's organizations, especially colleges and clubs, responded, and in many cases gifts came from persons who had experienced the benefit of radiumtherapy. In this way the "Marie Curie Radium Fund" of more than one hundred thousand dollars was collected.

据梅洛尼记述，仪式前一夜又出了岔子：文件要把这一克镭放在居里夫人个人名下。她读完说不行。这一克镭代表很多钱，可它更代表美国的妇女，不是给她的，是给科学的。她身体不好，随时可能死；女儿伊夫尚未成年，一旦她去世，镭就会进她的遗产，由两个女儿分掉。她要求当晚就把文件办好，因为第二天就要接收镭。于是那个闷热的五月夜晚，虽然已经很晚，他们还是请到律师，照她自拟的草稿写好文件。她在动身去华盛顿前签了字：她死后，这一克镭归巴黎的镭研究所，供居里实验室专用。第二天在白宫，哈定总统交给她的是一把小金钥匙。

As Meloney tells it, on the eve of the ceremony there was one more snag: the papers were to put this gramme of radium in Marie Curie's own name. Marie Curie read them and said it must not be left that way. The gramme represented a great deal of money, but more than that it represented the women of the country: it was not for her, it was for science. She was not well and might die any day. Her daughter Eve was not of legal age, and if she died the radium would go into her estate and be divided between her daughters. That was not its purpose; it had to be consecrated for all time to the use of science. The paper had to be fixed that night, because the next day she received the radium, and, she said, as Meloney reports it, "I might die tomorrow. Too much is at stake." So, late as it was on that hot May evening, a lawyer was secured and prepared the paper from a draft Marie Curie herself had written. She signed it before starting for Washington: in the event of her death the gramme of radium went to the Institut du Radium in Paris, for the exclusive use of the Laboratoire Curie. The next day at the White House, what she received from President Harding was the small golden key.

dispositions.rationale: 删去把设备不足定在“1921年”的说法，改为梅洛尼在1921年赠镭之前探访时得知的情况；中英同步。

evidence.quote: I also learned that Madame Curie's laboratory, although practically a new building, was without sufficient equipment

dispositions.rationale: 把“要靠募捐才能继续研究”改为梅洛尼发起募捐、希望借此让她继续研究，归因到梅洛尼的设想；中英同步。

evidence.quote: in this way to enable Madame Curie to go on with her work

dispositions.rationale: “没有地方干活”收窄为“缺合适的工作场所、缺人手，也缺钱”，与原文一致；中英同步。

evidence.quote: by the lack of a proper place to work in, by the lack of money and of personnel

dispositions.rationale: 改正归因：皮埃尔兼两处课，让他非常疲惫的是学生众多的P.C.N.教学；中英同步。

evidence.quote: and that in the P.C.N., with its very large number of students, fatigued him greatly.

dispositions.rationale: 改正先后顺序：梅洛尼先发起募捐，引言是后来写的。中文改为“梅洛尼（本书引言作者）曾在纽约发起这次募捐”，英文改为 who later wrote the book's introduction。

evidence.quote: May 20, 1921, when a gram of radium was presented to its discoverer by the women of America.

dispositions.rationale: 英文对居里夫人统一称“Marie Curie”：story.6、story.7 中单独的 Curie，story.0、context.2 中的 Marie，以及 hook.0 中的 Mme. Curie 均已替换。皮埃尔称 Pierre 或 Pierre Curie，均不致混淆，未改。中文原本统一，相应字段中文原样保留。

evidence.quote: "I? Oh, I have none," she corrected.

dispositions.rationale: 英文的 12 rue Cuvier 有证据支持，中文补上“居维叶街12号”及“供P.C.N.教学用”，使两种语言数字一致；英文原样保留。

evidence.quote: in the annex (12 rue Cuvier) of the Sorbonne, which served as teaching quarters for the P.C.N.
